paragraphs.text: The day that God has appointed for this judgment we do not know. But this is sure, that it will come upon men when they are not expecting it.
See Ac 1:7.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Returning to exhortations, he warns us who are enlightened with the knowledge of God, that it is our duty not to live securely in pleasures, lest we be suddenly taken in a dead sleep in pleasures. But contrary to this we are to have an eye to the Lord, and not allow ourselves to be oppressed with the cares of this world, for pleasures are fitting for the darkness of the night, and having an eye to the Lord is fitting for the light.
We must fight with faith and hope, and therefore we should certainly not lie snoring.
He urges us forward by setting a most certain hope of victory before us.
paragraphs.anchor: For God hath not appointed us

paragraphs.text: The death of Christ is a pledge of our victory, for he died so that we might be partakers of his life of power, indeed even while we live here.
We must not only watch ourselves, but we are also bound to stir up, and to strengthen and encourage one another.
We must have consideration of those who are appointed to the ministry of the word, and the government of the church of God, and who do their duty.
That you acknowledge and take them for such as they are, that is to say, men worthy to be greatly esteemed of among you.
paragraphs.label: b
paragraphs.anchor: know them which labour among you

paragraphs.text: In those things which pertain to God's service: so is the ecclesiastical function distinguished from civil authority, and true shepherds from wolves.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: So then, when this reason ceases, then must the honour cease.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: The maintenance of mutual harmony, is to be especially guarded.
paragraphs.anchor: And be at peace among yourselves

paragraphs.text: We must have consideration of every man, and the remedy must be applied according to the disease.
That keep not their rank or standing.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Charity ought not to be overcome by any injuries.
paragraphs.anchor: See that none render evil for

paragraphs.text: A quiet and appeased mind is nourished with continual prayers, giving regard to the will of God.
An acceptable thing to God, and such as he approves well of.
paragraphs.label: f
paragraphs.anchor: will of God in Christ Jesus

paragraphs.text: The sparks of the Spirit of God that are kindled in us, are nourished by daily hearing the word of God: but true doctrine must be diligently distinguished from false.
The explaining and interpreting of the word of God.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: A general conclusion, that we waiting for the coming of Christ, do give ourselves to pureness in mind, will, and body, through the grace and strength of the Spirit of God.
Whatever has but the very show of evil, abstain from it.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Separate you from the world, and make you holy to himself through his Spirit, in Christ, in whom alone you will attain to that true peace.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: The good will and power of God is a sure strengthening and encouragement against all difficulties, of which we have a sure witness in our calling.

Always one, and ever like himself, who indeed performs whatever he promises. And an effectual calling is nothing else but a right declaring and true setting forth of God's will: and therefore the salvation of the elect, is safe and sure.
paragraphs.label: k
paragraphs.anchor: Faithful is he that calleth you

paragraphs.text: Who will also make you perfect.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: The last part of the epistle, in which with most authoritative charge he commends both himself and this epistle to them.
